strategy.summary: Reproduce pandas GH#67945 (fix for overlaps() with empty Interval): ensure a test expecting empty intervals to never overlap fails on the buggy revision and passes on the fixed revision, using the project's own interval overlap tests (scalar and/or array) that assert all-empty overlap results are False.

build_commands: python -m pip install -U pip setuptools wheel
pinned_because: NumPy is numerically relevant but the evidence provides no documented version constraint; choose a modern stable NumPy compatible with the pandas revision under test (do not rely on a specific version pin from the evidence).
No documented constraint/era ceiling is provided for Cython; install latest compatible Cython for source builds per README.
No documented constraint/era ceiling is provided for python-dateutil; install via pandas extras/deps normally.

strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/arrays/interval/test_overlaps.py::TestOverlaps::test_overlaps_empty (the parametrized test that constructs interval_container from tuples and an empty Interval(start+shift, start+shift, empty_closed), then asserts result == np.array([False, False, False]) for overlaps(container, empty)).
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy pandas revision (commit 4bcadf56f045), running the test command above results in an assertion failure because interval_container.overlaps(empty) returns at least one True element (e.g., for empty_closed='right' with container constructed from tuples, the buggy behavior is described in the PR text as True in some cases). On the fixed revision (the PR merge commit after 4bcadf56f045), the same test passes because overlaps with empty intervals returns all-False for empty_closed in {'left','right','neither'}, matching expected = [False, False, False].
strategy.numerical_probe: Not used as a standalone probe; the test itself is the oracle via boolean array equality.
risks: Version pin risk: the evidence does not provide any documented NumPy/Python/Cython constraints; if the bug is present only under certain library/build combinations, it may not transition reliably. However the test strategy relies on pandas’ own interval semantics and should fail/pass across typical builds if the bug exists in that pandas revision.

Platform/toolchain risk: if scalar/array overlap behavior depends on compiled code paths (Cython) and the build fails or falls back differently, outcomes may vary; ensure a successful editable build as per README.

API-shape risk: the array test checks IntervalArray/constructor.from_tuples behavior; if the bug only affects scalar Interval.overlaps (or only affects array), you may need to run the scalar test instead (see alternative test command in oracle/rationale).

Empty-vs-point semantic risk: the test uses Interval(start+shift, start+shift, empty_closed) with empty_closed in {'left','right','neither'}; do not change that pattern to Interval(..., ..., 'both'), which would represent a point per the issue text (and would legitimately overlap).

oracle.reference_source: PR#67945 description/whatsnew: 'empty intervals contain no points at all, so they never overlap'; specifically added tests expect empty interval overlaps to be False for all closures.
oracle.why: The test asserts exact boolean equality: expected np.array([False, False, False]) equals the result from overlaps(container, empty). It does not use numeric tolerances.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: Fails the assertion tm.assert_numpy_array_equal(result, expected) because overlaps(container, empty) returns at least one True element for some empty_closed (the PR text gives examples where empty_closed='right' or 'neither' yields True for the buggy revision).
strategy.passes_on_fixed: Passes tm.assert_numpy_array_equal(result, expected) because overlaps(container, empty) returns [False, False, False] for empty_closed in ['left','right','neither'], and scalar assertions also hold (not required if array test suffices).
